findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded during controller requests, so fallback translations are missing in jobs/mailers
findings.body: The new fallback mechanism depends on `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` being called to eagerly load the user's locale, `SiteSetting.default_locale`, and `:en` (because the translate accelerator only lazy-loads `config.locale`). This call was added only in `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Any code path that translates outside of a controller request — Sidekiq/scheduled jobs, email rendering (`UserNotifications`), oneboxing, rake tasks, console — will translate with only the current locale's yml loaded. When a key is missing in that locale, the fallbacks backend looks up the default locale and `:en`, finds nothing loaded, and renders 'translation missing' instead of the English fallback. `ensure_loaded!` needs to be invoked wherever `I18n.locale=` is set (e.g., in the jobs/mailer code paths), not just in the controller.

findings.title: Custom fallback list drops parent-language fallbacks for regional locales (e.g. pt_BR no longer falls back to pt)
findings.body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` returns exactly `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en]`. The standard `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` behavior (which `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` provided and this PR removes) decomposes regional locales so that `pt_BR` falls back to `pt` before hitting the default. With this change, a user with locale `pt_BR` (or `zh_TW`, `nb_NO`-style tags) will see English for every key that exists in the base `pt` translation but not in `pt_BR`, which is a user-visible regression for regional locales. The TODO comment even acknowledges per-language ordering is needed; at minimum the list should insert the language-only parent (`locale.to_s.split('_').first`) between the locale and the site default.

findings.title: @loaded_locales is read outside the load mutex and can be nil on first translate
findings.body: In `translate`, `@loaded_locales.include?(config.locale)` is evaluated without synchronization and without the nil guard that the newly added `ensure_loaded!` has (`@loaded_locales ||= []`). `@loaded_locales` is only initialized in `reload!`; if `translate` is invoked before any `reload!` (or after a direct `load_locale` call from another thread partially completes), the first check raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'include?' for nil`. More generally the check-then-load pattern here is unsynchronized, so two threads can race through `load_locale` — the mutex inside `load_locale` makes the double-load harmless, but the nil read is not protected. `translate` should use the same `@loaded_locales ||= []` guard (or route through `ensure_loaded!`).

findings.title: FallbackLocaleList recomputes SiteSetting.default_locale on every translation fallback lookup
findings.body: Because `FallbackLocaleList#[]` is overridden without memoization, every translation lookup that misses the primary locale triggers a `SiteSetting.default_locale` read (which hits the site settings cache/provider) and allocates a new array. Under load this happens per missing-key translation. Consider caching the computed list per locale (e.g., storing into the Hash) and invalidating when the default locale setting changes.
